words.ex: Her recovery is a testimony to her effort.
use: The teacher's testimony supported the student.
교사의 증언이 그 학생에게 힘이 됐다.
His calm testimony convinced the jury.
그의 침착한 증언이 배심원을 설득했다.
mcq: Her success is a testimony to years of practice.
Her success is a testimony of to practice.
Her success testimonies years of practice.
Testimony her success is years to.
words.note: a testimony to = ~을 입증하는 것. 격식 있는 칭찬 표현!

words.ex: Anyone who saw it can testify.
words.exko: 그걸 본 사람은 누구든 증언할 수 있어요.
use: The expert testified about the child's needs.
전문가가 그 아이의 필요에 대해 증언했다.
I can testify to his dedication.
그의 헌신은 제가 보증합니다.
mcq: She testified before the committee.
She testified in front to the committee.
She testimonied before the committee.
The committee testified her before.
words.note: testify before + 위원회/법정. 교육청 회의 상황에도 응용 가능!

words.ex: Some students are more vulnerable to stress.
use: We protect the most vulnerable children first.
가장 취약한 아이들을 먼저 보호한다.
Sharing feelings makes us vulnerable — and stronger.
감정을 나누면 약해지지만 동시에 강해진다.
mcq: Young children are vulnerable to noise.
Young children are vulnerable at noise.
Young children vulnerable to noise.
Noise is vulnerable to young children.
words.note: vulnerable to + 요인. 특수교육 현장에서 핵심 단어!

words.ex: It's a myth that ADHD means low intelligence.
words.exko: ADHD가 낮은 지능을 뜻한다는 건 잘못된 통념이에요.
use: The workshop busted myths about autism.
그 워크숍은 자폐에 대한 통념을 깼다.
Every culture has creation myths.
모든 문화에는 창조 신화가 있다.
mcq: It's a myth that sugar causes hyperactivity.
It's a myth story about sugar causes.
The myth is sugar that causing.
Sugar myths that hyperactivity causes.
words.note: It's a myth that... — 잘못된 통념을 바로잡을 때 쓰는 강력한 틀!

words.ex: The rumor turned out to be false.
words.exko: 그 소문은 사실이 아닌 걸로 밝혀졌어요.
use: Rumor has it that the school is expanding.
소문에 의하면 학교가 확장한대요.
Don't spread rumors about colleagues.
동료에 대한 소문을 퍼뜨리지 마세요.
mcq: Rumor has it that he's transferring.
Rumor has it to he's transferring.
Rumor is having that he transfers.
It rumors he that transferring is.
words.note: Rumor has it that... = 소문으로는. 회화에서 진짜 자주 나와요!

words.ex: Keep children away from open flames.
use: The campfire flames danced in the dark.
모닥불 불꽃이 어둠 속에서 일렁였다.
Simmer the soup over a low flame.
수프를 약불에서 뭉근히 끓이세요.
mcq: The flames spread quickly through the building.
The flames spread quick through building.
The flame fires spread quickly.
Quickly the spreading flames building through.
words.note: flames(복수) = 화염. 안전 교육 필수 단어!

words.ex: X-rays use a small amount of radiation.
use: He's receiving radiation treatment.
그는 방사선 치료를 받고 있다.
The screen filter reduces blue light radiation.
그 필터는 블루라이트를 줄여준다.
mcq: The device emits almost no radiation.
The device emits almost no radiations.
The device radiates no emit.
No radiation emits the device almost.
words.note: radiation은 셀 수 없는 명사. emit radiation = 방사선을 내뿜다.

words.ex: Parents donated books to the classroom.
use: The alumni donated funds for the new gym.
동문들이 새 체육관 기금을 기부했다.
Consider donating your time, not just money.
돈만이 아니라 시간을 기부하는 것도 생각해 보세요.
mcq: They donated supplies to the school.
They donated supplies for to the school.
They donated the school at supplies.
The school donated them supplies to.
words.note: donate A to B. donate time(시간 기부)이라는 확장도!

words.ex: Some mushrooms are deadly.
use: The virus can be deadly for the elderly.
그 바이러스는 노인에게 치명적일 수 있다.
She gave me a deadly serious look.
그녀가 아주 진지한 표정으로 나를 봤다.
mcq: Peanut allergies can be deadly.
Peanut allergies can be deathly killed.
Peanut allergies can deadly.
Deadly can peanut allergies be it.
words.note: deadly는 -ly로 끝나지만 형용사! 알레르기 안전 교육에 중요.

words.ex: The chocolate melted in my pocket.
use: The kids watched the ice melt in the sun.
아이들이 햇빛에 얼음이 녹는 걸 지켜봤다.
His kind words melted her anger away.
그의 다정한 말에 그녀의 화가 녹아내렸다.
mcq: The snowman melted by noon.
The snowman melted himself by noon.
The snowman made melt by noon.
By noon melting the snowman was gone it.
words.note: melt = 녹다. 과학 수업 시연에도, 감정 표현에도!

words.ex: The twins resemble each other closely.
use: His teaching style resembles my old mentor's.
그의 교육 방식은 옛 멘토와 비슷하다.
The symptoms resemble a common cold.
그 증상은 감기와 비슷하다.
mcq: This case resembles one from last year.
This case resembles to one from last year.
This case resembles with last year one.
This case is resembled last year.
words.note: resemble + 대상 바로 — 전치사 금지! 시험 단골 포인트.

words.ex: The new students are eager to learn.
use: He's eager to show what he can do.
그는 자기 능력을 보여주고 싶어 한다.
Eager hands went up all over the class.
교실 곳곳에서 손이 번쩍번쩍 올라왔다.
mcq: She's eager to join the program.
She's eager for join the program.
She's eager joining the program.
She eagers to join program.
words.note: eager to + 동사. 학생 추천서에 쓰기 좋은 단어!

words.ex: Is it ethical to use AI for grading?
use: Teachers face ethical questions daily.
교사는 매일 윤리적 질문에 부딪힌다.
The company promotes ethical business practices.
그 회사는 윤리 경영을 추구한다.
mcq: We discussed the ethical issues involved.
We discussed the ethic issues involved.
We discussed ethically the issues.
The issues ethical discussed we.
words.note: ethical(형용사) vs ethics(윤리학·명사) 구분!

words.ex: He was diagnosed with dyslexia at seven.
words.exko: 그는 일곱 살에 난독증 진단을 받았어요.
use: Early diagnosis makes a huge difference.
조기 진단이 큰 차이를 만든다.
The doctor diagnosed the problem quickly.
의사가 문제를 빠르게 진단했다.
mcq: She was diagnosed with ADHD last year.
She was diagnosed by ADHD last year.
She diagnosed ADHD to her last year.
ADHD diagnosed her with last year.
words.note: be diagnosed with + 질환명. 특수교육 서류·상담의 핵심 표현!

words.ex: Watch for subtle signs of frustration.
use: The change in his behavior was subtle.
그의 행동 변화는 미묘했다.
She has a subtle sense of humor.
그녀는 은근한 유머 감각이 있다.
mcq: There were subtle signs of improvement.
There were subtly signs of improvement.
Subtle there were improvement signs of.
The signs subtled of improvement.
words.note: subtle — b는 묵음(/서틀/)! 관찰 기록에 자주 쓰는 단어.

words.ex: Clapping helps kids feel the rhythm.
use: Find your own study rhythm.
자기만의 공부 리듬을 찾으세요.
The rhythm of the poem is easy to follow.
그 시의 리듬은 따라가기 쉽다.
mcq: Music therapy uses rhythm and repetition.
Music therapy uses rhythm beats and repetition.
Rhythm uses music therapy repetition and.
The repetition rhythms music therapy.
words.note: rhythm — 철자 어려운 단어 대표(모음이 y 하나)! 발음 도전각.

words.ex: We utilize visual aids in every lesson.
words.exko: 저희는 모든 수업에 시각 자료를 활용해요.
use: The app utilizes AI to adjust difficulty.
그 앱은 AI를 활용해 난이도를 조절한다.
Utilize your strengths in the interview.
면접에서 당신의 강점을 활용하세요.
mcq: Teachers utilize games to engage students.
Teachers utilize of games to engage.
Teachers utilizes game for engaging.
Games utilize teachers to engagement.
words.note: utilize = use의 격식 버전. 보고서·계획서에서 빛나는 단어!

words.ex: I do my grocery shopping on Sundays.
use: The grocery store closes at 11.
그 식료품점은 11시에 닫는다.
We taught money skills using grocery lists.
장보기 목록으로 돈 개념을 가르쳤다.
mcq: I need to pick up some groceries.
I need to pick up some grocery.
I need to grocery some pickings.
Some groceries need to pick I up.
words.note: 장 본 물건들 = groceries(복수)! 생활 자립 교육에 딱 맞는 단어.

words.ex: We planted a small vegetable patch.
use: He's going through a rough patch.
그는 힘든 시기를 지나고 있다.
Patch the hole before it gets bigger.
구멍이 커지기 전에 메우세요.
mcq: She's been through a rough patch lately.
She's been through a rough patch time lately.
A rough patch has been she through.
Lately rough patches through she has.
words.note: a rough patch = 힘든 시기. 학생 상담에서 부드럽게 쓸 수 있는 표현!

words.ex: It was a seemingly simple question.
use: Seemingly small habits shape big outcomes.
사소해 보이는 습관이 큰 결과를 만든다.
The seemingly shy student loves the stage.
수줍어 보이는 그 학생이 무대를 좋아한다.
mcq: The task was seemingly easy but tricky.
The task was seeming easy but tricky.
The task seemingly was easy tricking.
Seemingly the easy task but was tricky.
words.note: seemingly + 형용사 = 겉보기엔 ~한. 반전을 만들 때 쓰는 부사!
